analysis.title: Global Economic Outlook & Strategy: The Global Economy's Tenuous Balance—Resilience Amid Uncertainty
key_insights: Citi sees 2026 global growth at 2.7% (slightly stronger than last month) and 2027 at 2.8%, as pressures from the Iran conflict eventually moderate. Brent is at $115/bbl, near this year's peaks.
Headline inflation is seen at 3.4% in 2026, up from 2.8% in 2025, and 3.0% in 2027 assuming some oil moderation. Oil is up about 60% since February, jet fuel up 100% and diesel up 110%.

Core inflation pressure persists from transport costs and supply chain damage (aluminum, petrochemicals, fertilizers). Citi's 2026 core inflation forecasts are at least 0.5 ppt higher than in February for Brazil, Australia, Korea, the euro area and Thailand.
Since the Iran conflict began, 10-year yields are up 175 bp in France, over 100 bp in the US and UK, and 75 bp in Japan, Germany and Canada. Markets other than France have stabilized in recent weeks.

Citi attributes the yield rise to pressure on the savings pool: US Treasury issuance of $2 trillion or more a year, other sovereigns needing $1 trillion or more, and AI capex projected to exceed $3.5 trillion by 2030. Term and risk premiums are also rising.

Long-term breakevens are little changed for the US and about 30 bp higher for the euro area and Japan, so oil volatility may be lifting term premiums through inflation uncertainty rather than expected inflation.

France: IMF projections have the deficit near 4% of GDP and debt heading toward 120% of GDP. Presidential and likely parliamentary elections in spring/early summer 2027 leave little prospect of restoring market confidence before then.

Citi is broadly bullish on the AI buildout and expects it to continue well into the next decade, with productivity gains about 2-3 years away. It watches three risks: financial disruption (late-1990s analogy), eroding political support (under 30% of US voters back the current pace), and a severe cyber event.
Across 27 major central banks Citi expects 5 to ease, 16 to hike and 6 to hold in 2026. For 2027 it expects 11 hiking and 11 cutting.

Fed: held in October, markets lean toward a December hike. Citi expects one more hike in December and cuts later in 2027. Core PCE is running at about 3%. Fed Chair Warsh gives no forward guidance and has been more hawkish. The ECB, BoE and BoJ are all expected to hike by year-end.

US rates: Citi is neutral on duration but constructive on the 5-year point. It expects Treasury to cut long-end issuance in favor of bills at the November 4 refunding, and a very light bull flattening if a Democratic 'blue wave' occurs at the midterms.

Core Europe and EMU spreads: Citi anchors the 10-year Bund at 3.4% and expects the ECB to hike twice more to 3% by March. It expects the 10-year OAT-Bund spread to average 175 bp around the French elections and stay above 100 bp long term.

UK gilts: Citi sees improving sentiment on fiscal credibility, with 10-year gilt targets of 4.7% for end-2027 and 4.25% for end-2028. It expects the BoE to hike in November and again in February 2027.
Japan: a December BoJ hike is highly probable, with terminal rate 2.0%. The 10-year JGB retreated below 2.8% from a peak above 3.0%.

Commodities: base case (60%) is Strait of Hormuz flows normalizing by year-end, with a $75/bbl Brent 0-3m target. The bull case (30%) is disruption persisting or a major escalation, taking Brent to about $120.
Gold: Citi sees a favorable risk skew, with up to $4,800/oz near term and $5,000/oz by early 2027, and dip buying around $4,000 as support. Silver is forecast at $75 in 0-3m.
Copper and aluminum: Citi is near-term neutral (copper $14-15k/t, aluminum $3,000/t) with a bullish tail skew. It is structurally bullish on tin ($60k/t base case).

Global equities: Citi expects further earnings-driven upside to mid-2027. 2026E global EPS growth is +37% and 2027E is +17%, a drop of about 20 pp, with tech responsible for 70% of 2027 profit growth. It stays overweight global IT and the US, and neutral Europe.
Positioning: equity positioning turned broadly bearish after last week's rotation, with fresh short selling in the Nasdaq and S&P 500. Citi's Levkovich Index remains in 'Euphoria'.
FX: Citi lowers its 0-3m EURUSD forecast to 1.1050 and keeps 6-12m at 1.13, citing unresolved European tail risks, Fed-ECB divergence favoring the USD, and elevated energy prices.

Brazil: Lula's surprise runoff win on Oct 25 drove a market sell-off and weaker currency, likely halting Copom's easing cycle on Nov 4. Australia: the RBA is seen hiking 25bp on Nov 3 (market probability moved from 30% to 68%). New Zealand: the RBNZ is expected to hike to 3.00%.

China Q3 GDP was 4.5% YoY. Citi expects no new stimulus this year but sees 2027 as more challenging, with 20 bp of rate cuts and a RMB2tn deficit expansion. India: September CPI was 5.54%, with 2x25bp RBI hikes expected in December and February. South Korea: BoK hikes expected in November and February.

earnings_insights: Global 2026E EPS growth expectations have been revised up about 20 pp YTD to +37% (consensus estimate). Consensus 2027E global EPS growth is +17%, a deceleration of about 20 pp.
Tech is expected to account for 70% of global profit growth in 2027E, which could make it one of the narrowest EPS growth years on record.

risk_factors: Sustainability of the AI boom and the risk of financial bubble dynamics
Eroding US political support for AI, including data center moratorium calls
A severe AI-enabled cyber event or a rogue AI model
French fiscal and political stress spreading to Belgium, Italy and the UK
Persistent oil prices from the Iran conflict and Strait of Hormuz disruption
Central bank tightening and rising neutral rates
Concentration of 2027 EPS growth in tech
Brazil fiscal credibility after Lula's win
Possible early UK election raising gilt risk premium

geopolitical: US-Iran conflict continues, with Strait of Hormuz flows disrupted and an economic blockade on Iran.
French fiscal and political stress ahead of spring 2027 presidential and parliamentary elections.
German coalition tension, with Chancellor Merz weakened after three state election losses.
Brazil's Lula won the Oct 25 runoff over Flavio Bolsonaro, who has not recognized the result.
US-Canada trade tension: 50% US tariffs on some Canadian goods and Canadian retaliation.
US midterm elections with AI as a political issue.

tension_points.bull_case: Corporate sector solid, labor markets firm, consumers still spending, PMIs strong on AI-driven electronics, and 2026 growth at 2.7%.
tension_points.bear_case: Brent at $115, a sovereign yield surge, AI sustainability concerns and weak confidence indicators.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A shock large enough to dislodge growth, such as an AI-related financial disruption or severe oil escalation (bull case Brent about $120).

tension_points.bull_case: Enterprise demand is an imperative, spending is insensitive to rates, and investment should continue well into the next decade.
tension_points.bear_case: Bubble and mispricing risk resembling the late 1990s, eroding political support (under 30% of voters back the current pace), and cyber risk.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Policy turning less supportive after the midterms, especially if a Democrat wins the presidency in 2028.

tension_points.bull_case: Base case (60%): flows normalize by year-end and Brent falls to $75, supporting gold and easing inflation.
tension_points.bear_case: Bull case (30%) for oil: disruption persists through next year or escalation hits infrastructure, taking Brent to about $120.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Flows through the Strait of Hormuz failing to improve during Q4 2026.
